title: Rebar Calculator
seoTitle: Rebar Calculator for Slabs and Footings
metaDescription: Estimate rebar sticks, linear feet, weight, tie points, and chairs for a slab or footing grid in US units, with a lap-aware cut list and CRSI bar weights.
secondaryKeywords: how many rebar chairs do i need
intent: Estimate rebar count, linear feet, sticks, weight, and tie points for a slab or footing grid at a chosen spacing.
registerRow: Keyword Register: rebar calculator (Volume 2, Competition ease 4, Ad value 2, Fit 5, Priority 16)
intro: Enter your slab or footing size, bar size, and grid spacing to get the number of rebar sticks to buy, a cut list for each direction, the total weight, and how many ties and chairs to pick up. Long bars are spliced with the lap length you choose, so the stick count matches how the grid actually goes together.
chartTitle: Sticks to buy at other grid spacings (same slab, bar, and waste)
uniqueAddition: Lap-aware stick count with a cut list (bars per direction, cut length, sticks per direction, lap splices), purchase weight from CRSI unit weights, a bar-size weight table, and a line chart of sticks needed at 12, 16, 18, 24, and 36 in spacing.

inputs.name: length
inputs.label: Length
inputs.help: 1 to 100 ft. The long side of the slab or footing. Use decimals for inches (20 ft 6 in = 20.5).

inputs.name: width
inputs.label: Width
inputs.help: 1 to 100 ft. For a footing, this is the footing's width.

inputs.name: barSize
inputs.label: Bar size
inputs.help: Use the size on your plan. Weights are ASTM A615 values published by CRSI.

inputs.name: spacing
inputs.label: Spacing, each direction
inputs.help: 6 to 36 in, center to center. Must match your plan or local requirements. 18 in is only a starting point, not a code approval.

inputs.name: cover
inputs.label: Edge cover
inputs.help: 1 to 6 in. Gap between the bar ends and the edge of the form, on every side. 3 in is our assumption, not a verified code value.

inputs.name: stickLength
inputs.label: Stick length
inputs.help: 10 to 40 ft. The length your store sells. 20 ft is common but check; many stores also stock 10 ft sticks.

inputs.name: lap
inputs.label: Lap length
inputs.help: 0 to 60 in. How far two bars overlap where a run needs more than one stick. 20 in is about 40 bar diameters for #4, a common rule of thumb we haven't verified against ACI 318. Use your plan's number.

inputs.name: chairSpacing
inputs.label: Chair spacing
inputs.help: 12 to 72 in, each direction. Rough estimate only; follow the chair maker's guidance.

inputs.name: waste
inputs.label: Waste allowance
inputs.help: 0 to 20%. Extra sticks for bad cuts and bent bars. 5% is our starting estimate, not a published figure.

sources.title: CRSI Product Catalog, Winter 2025 (Concrete Reinforcing Steel Institute): ASTM A615 bar sizes, nominal diameters, and unit weights
